name: Trogir Old Town
tagline: UNESCO island core of marble lanes
description: The tiny island heart of Trogir, a dense UNESCO warren of marble streets, Venetian palaces, the Cathedral of St Lawrence and the seafront riva. Beautiful and atmospheric, but lively, touristic and pricey through the summer months.
bestFor: Culture lovers wanting atmosphere, walkability and cafe work in a stunning setting
cons: Crowded and noisy in peak summer

name: Trogir Mainland (Travarica)
tagline: Practical mainland side near the market
description: The mainland district just across the northern bridge, home to the town market, bus station, shops and everyday services. Quieter and better value than the island, with easy walking access to the old town and quick connections onward.
bestFor: Nomads wanting value, amenities and quick transport while staying near the old town
pros: Better rental value than the island
Close to market and bus station
cons: Less charm than the old town

name: Ciovo (Okrug Gornji)
tagline: Beachy island side across the bridge
description: The larger island of Ciovo, reached by a short bridge, with beaches, coves and resort-style apartments around Okrug Gornji and Slatine. Calmer and more residential than the old town, ideal for swimming, quiet work and sea views.
bestFor: Nomads craving quiet apartments, sea access and calmer focused work near beaches
pros: Good apartment choice and sea views
cons: Spread out, sometimes needs a car

name: Seget Donji
description: A laid-back seaside village a short walk or drive west of Trogir, with a marina, waterfront promenade and affordable apartments. It offers a calmer, more local pace while keeping the old town and airport comfortably within reach.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting a calm local base close to Trogir and the airport
cons: Walk or drive needed for old town
